messages:
deploy-bot: [deploy] Canary rollout 2026.03.18-rc8 reported postdeploy failures
deploy-bot: service=renderer-canary, env=canary-us-west-2, pods_unready=2/3, reason=CrashLoopBackOff, recent_event=EnvOverrideDetected
maria: any more context on the EnvOverrideDetected tag? :eyes:
alex: looks like the chart default for `cache.mode` changed in the chart's v1.4.0 -> v1.5.0, staging had an explicit `values.yaml` override but the release omitted it for canary, so canary got the new default (in-memory) while prod/staging retained `redis` in values
sre-jordan: so staging != canary != prod then. not great during rollout. can we roll back the canary image or patch the values?
devex-anya: quick mitigation: hard-pin `--set cache.mode=redis` in the helm upgrade for this canary, push a tiny patch release. we should also add a lint check to prevent implicit chart defaults changing behavior without a values override
kevin: what's the impact surface? does in-memory cache cause data loss for sessions? any customer-facing errors?
alex: hitting 502s for a subset of requests that hit session code paths — memory-backed cache has evictions; renders depend on KV prefixes set via `REDWOOD_KV_PREFIX`, which is also different between environments due to an undocumented override in staging overlay
maria: wait, undocumented override? where was that set?
alex: in the old staging kustomize overlay — someone added `env: REDWOOD_KV_PREFIX=stg-` as a stopgap last year, but it never made it into the Helm values or the chart defaults. prod doesn't have it. canary got default chart value AND the new image which expects the prefix to be present -> mismatch causing key lookups to fail
sre-jordan: immediate plan: revert the canary to previous image tag (2026.03.10-stable) to get service healthy. then coordinate a follow-up to decide canonical behavior (chart default vs explicit values). rollback approved? :+1: reactions from infra oncall
kevin: approved. schedule rollback outside the customer-impacting change window? or do it now if it's quick?
maria: it's blocking, I'd prefer immediate rollback. we can run the rollback job and monitor for 5m then promote again once we have explicit values
devex-anya: I'll prepare a patch PR that adds explicit `cache.mode: redis` and documents `REDWOOD_KV_PREFIX` in chart README and release notes. also add a helm-lint CI check that fails if a chart default changes a functional behavior without a minor/major bump
alex: PR draft: https://git.internal/redwood/charts/renderer/pulls/412 - includes values snippet and test
alex: values snippet:
```
cache:
  mode: redis
  redis:
    host: redis-main.redwood.svc.cluster.local
    ttl: 3600
env:
  REDWOOD_KV_PREFIX: "stg-" # explicit to match staging overlay
```
sre-jordan: rollback job queued: `deploy-bot rollback renderer-canary --to-tag=2026.03.10-stable` scheduled at 1865432128 by deploy-bot
deploy-bot: rollback started: job_id=rb-20260318-77, initiating pod replacement now
kevin: after rollback, can we add a release note blurb and a follow-up RFC for alignment? also consider pinning chart major for any breaking default changes
maria: yes. devex-anya, please add the release note and tag the release with `postmortem:required` if we decide changes beyond docs are needed
devex-anya: will do. I'll also coordinate a short postmortem doc and assign owners
deploy-bot: rollback complete, renderer-canary pods healthy 3/3 at 1865432145, monitoring for 5m
sre-jordan: monitoring green. leaving canary at stable image for now. follow-up actions: 1) merge PR with explicit values, 2) add helm-lint CI, 3) run a controlled canary with explicit values and observe 24h, 4) update release notes + RFC if we change chart defaults. assigning owners in the PR comments
kevin: thanks all. quick win: add a checklist item in our release playbook to verify no implicit chart-default behavior changed between chart versions during upgrades
maria: noted. thanks team :thumbsup:
